title: Nonnegative Jacobian formula and integrability on coordinate domains
statement: Use $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $m\geq1$, let $D,D^{\prime}\subseteq\mathbf R^m$ be open, let $F:D\to D^{\prime}$ be a $C^1$ diffeomorphism (a bijection with both $F$ and $F^{-1}$ continuously differentiable), and let $S\subseteq D$ be Borel. Write $J_F(y)=|\det DF(y)|$ and use Lebesgue measure. For every function $H:D^{\prime}\to[0,\infty]$, the nonnegative Lebesgue integrals, allowed to be infinite, satisfy $$\int_{F(S)}H(x)\,dx=\int_S J_F(y)H(F(y))\,dy.$$ No measurability of $H$ is required for this lower-integral identity. Moreover, for every integer $q\geq0$ and every function $h:D^{\prime}\to\mathbf R^q$, one has $$h\text{ is Bochner integrable on }F(S)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y\longmapsto J_F(y)h(F(y))\text{ is Bochner integrable on }S.$$ Bochner integrable means strongly measurable up to a null set with finite integral of its norm.
